name: the touch twins are ignored: a phone reads the desktop switch
why: On a touch-primary device the _on_touch twin REPLACES the plain switch (org/non-MB-sites.org): the plain switches are on by default, and on touch an enabled source turns every tap into 'open the window', taking ordinary link navigation away from a phone.
grep: a tap on a release link opens the release window

name: the touch twins are ignored: the desktop switch on still opens windows on a phone
why: The same defect seen from the other side: with the twin at its default (off) a tap must open the page, whatever the desktop switch says.
grep: with the touch twin at its default

name: the touch twins are ignored: a tap on a link to another site is the engine's on a phone
why: The external side of the same defect: with sa_pop_ext on and its twin at the default, the engine must stay out of a tap.

name: a desktop reads the touch twins
why: The twins have no effect on a desktop browser: there the plain switches, on by default, decide.

name: the page-wide scope ignores its touch twin
why: sa_pop_mb_page_on_touch, not sa_pop_mb_page, decides on touch whether a link outside the tables is the engine's.
grep: outside the tables, the tap follows

name: the external source ignores its touch twin
why: sa_pop_ext_on_touch, not sa_pop_ext, decides on touch whether a tap on a link to another site opens the window.
grep: a tap on a link to another site opens its window
